newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ housing data negative for interest rates - BTNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ housing data negative for interest rates - BTNZ.

text.p: Bankers Trust economists said on Thursday that Real Estate Institute of New Zealand figures were negative for interest rates and positive for the currency.
"It highlights the risk that strengthening activity will prompt the Reserve Bank of New Zealand to tighten sooner rather than later," they said.
Median house prices increased to $159,000 in January from $154,000 in December and the number of sales rose to 7,815 from 5,741.
BT said the size of the increase in both prices and sales pointed to a considerable firming in the housing market.
Recent Valuation New Zealand figures and the ASB quarterly housing survey backed up the REINZ data.

There is a 6-9 month lag in house price data before it feeds into the Consumer Price Index, but the latest data could be expected to push up the Reserve Bank's forecast for inflation in the June and September 1997 quarters, BTNZ said.
BTNZ believes the RBNZ will maintain an easing bias until the middle of this year before it swings into tightening mode.

"Some of the recent data, particularly the strength of the housing market, increases the risk the RBNZ tightens earlier than expected -- or, at the very least, confirms the market-led tightening we have had in the last week or so.
"However, the RBNZ is not yet likely to see the data as conclusive on the need for an early tightening."
Next week's wage data will be critical in determining what stance the RBNZ takes in its March forecasts.
